newsitem.title: NORWAY: NORDIC SKIING-DAEHLIE HELPS NORWAY TO BRILLIANT RELAY WIN.
newsitem.headline: NORDIC SKIING-DAEHLIE HELPS NORWAY TO BRILLIANT RELAY WIN.

text.p: Bjorn Daehlie played a key role in a brilliant demonstration by Norway who cruised to an impressive triumph on home snow in the men's relay at the Nordic skiing world championships on Friday.
Cheered on by a huge, 80.000 crowd, the Norwegians were in a class of their own, leading from start to finish before clocking a winning time of one hour 37 minutes 06.10 seconds.
Finland and Italy, who came second and third respectively, were never able to match the formidable pace set by the Norwegians and finished over two minutes late.

Sture Sivertsen, the first Norwegian to set off in the 4x10-km race, moved in front straight away before handing over to Erling Jevne, who allowed his team to reach halfway with Finland trailing by 24 seconds.

Daehlie, the winner of two golds already in the 10-day festival, put the issue beyond doubt by increasing Norway's lead to one minute and 43 seconds after completing his two laps of a bumpy, five-km circuit.
The last 10 kms were merely a formality for Thomas Alsgaard, who took plenty of time to pick up a Norwegian flag in the finish straight which he waved until the line.
Jari Isometsae came a distant second as Finland took silver while Fulvio Valbusa outsprinted Russian Alexei Prokurorov to give Italy third place.

Norway's success was no surprise as they had won gold in the relay in the last two world championships but the overall strength of the Finnish team and the pride of Olympic champions Italy suggested a tough contest.
It was not to be as Norway recorded the biggest winning margin in a relay of a major competition for over 30 years.
"It turned out to be a parade march," said Alsgaard. "I was very happy to complete the relay."

Sivertsen, who gave his side an early lead by breaking away from Finn Harri Kirvesniemi, said the Norwegians had just the perfect skis for demanding conditions with a track covered by a thin layer of fresh snow.
"Those who waxed our skis deserve a medal," he said. "I didn't think Kirvesniemi would drop back like he did. Maybe I was going very fast."

After crossing the line, Alsgaard was met by Daehlie and Sivertsen, who lifted him up on their shoulders. Then the four Norwegians showed they had plenty of energy left by taking off their skis to run around the stadium.
''We wanted to thank the people for supporting us," Jevne said. "It was just incredible. They were shouting and dancing. It's a great feeling to race in such an atmosphere."

It was unclear if Daehlie would take part of the relay or take a rest ahead of Sunday's 50-km race. The winner of the 10-km classic and 15-km pursuit golds eventually decided to enter and he gave his all.

"It was fun," he said. "I had great skis and I was in top shape. I wasn't thinking about saving any strength for Sunday. I just went as fast as I could. When you get the kind of support whe had today, it makes you want to do the maximum."
